implementation_notes: Both halves are standard library, so no framework is needed: http.NewServeMux (with "GET /orders/{id}" patterns since Go 1.22) is the controller/dispatcher, a handler function is the worker that calls the service layer and builds a typed view value, and html/template's ExecuteTemplate/Execute is the render step; template.FuncMap entries and inner templates cover helper work, while middleware wraps the handler and therefore sits around the worker, not the view. Reach for chi or Gin (c.HTML) only when routing must compose large middleware stacks; when the response is JSON there is no view to select and plain handlers are the honest answer.
pitfalls: Execute streams as it renders: once it starts, the status line is already sent, so a template error yields a truncated 200 unless rendering goes to a bytes.Buffer first.
The error from Execute is easy to discard (many examples do); an unchecked render error turns a broken view into a silently empty page.
Passing map[string]any to templates gives up the typed field access that html/template escapes for; a view struct keeps the worker/view contract visible.
A handler must not stash *http.Request or its context in shared state - it is per-request, and goroutines outlive it.
